AWARD  Vide this award, the Tribunal shall decide the claim petition arising out of FIR No. 675/20, u/s 279/337/338 IPC, PS Tronica City, Ghaziabad, filed for the petitioner against the respondents as mentioned in the memo of parties.
FACTS OF THE CASE 1.

Briefly stated, the facts of the petition are that on 14.11.2020, at about 05:30 p.m., the petitioner Sunita Vaid alongwith her husband namely Satish Kumar Vaid was going from her in-law's village at Baghpat to her sister's house at Tronica City, on a motorcycle bearing registration no. PB35Y-1580.

It has been alleged that when the petitioner alongwith her husband reached near Sapna-2 Chowk,
Awaas Vikas Mandola, within the jurisdiction of PS Tronica City, a green colour Maruti ALTO K10 bearing registration no. DL3CCN-6433 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came from the wrong side and hit the afore-said motorcycle of the petitioner from front side with a great force.

It has been further alleged that the offending vehicle was being driven by its driver i.e. respondent no.
1 herein, at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without taking due caution.
Allegedly, the petitioner along with her husband as aforesaid fell down on the road after being hit by the offending vehicle and they sustained grievous injuries.

The petitioner and her husband were thereon taken to Air Force Hospital, Hindon Air Force Station, Ghaziabad, for primary treatment and thereafter the treatment continued in Base Hospital, Delhi Cantt.

Issue wise findings Issue no.1 Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 14.11.2020 at about 05:30 pm at Sapna-02 Chowk, Awaas Vikas Mandola within the jurisdiction of PS Tronica City Ghaziabad, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no.
DL3CCN6433 being driven by respondent no. 1/driver?
OPP 16.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities .

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP

In the present case, the petitioner has examined herself as PW-2 and her husband as PW1 to prove her contentions.

Both the said witnesses being the eye witnesses of the incident also, have categorically stated in their examination on oath that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent act of Respondent no. 1 as the latter was driving the offending vehicle in a very rash and negligent manner at a very high speed and that the offending vehicle had hit the vehicle of the petitioner from front side.
The said contentions are duly corroborated by the findings of the police as mentioned in the criminal case documents and no ground has been made out by the respondents to disbelieve the same.

18. Respondent no. 1 i.e. driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle and respondent no. 2 i.e.
Insurance Company, have neither impeached the testimony of PW-1 nor they have led any defence evidence to substantiate their claim that the accident was caused due to fault of the petitioner or her husband or that they have been falsely implicated in the present case.

The evidence of the star witness in this case i.e. PW-1 & PW2 on the aspect of rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 while driving the offending vehicle, has remained unimpeached and their testimony has to be accepted on its face value itself.

19. The very fact that R-1 has already been specifically arrayed as an accused in case FIR No. 675/20,
PS Tronica City, for the offences u/s 279/337/338 IPC Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.02.06 14:24:22 +0530 is itself a strong circumstance to support the above said testimony of PW-1 on these issues.

The copies of FIR, Site plan, seizure memos,
mechanical inspection, notice u/s 133 MV Act and charge sheet u/s 173 Cr.P.C also corroborate the oral testimony of PW1 & PW2.
20.

Besides the above, respondent no. 1 namely Uttam Rathi was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the depositions being made by PW-1 & PW2 regarding the above accident and its manner etc., but he has not done so.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
21.

sentences.text: In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that the offending vehicle was being driven by R-1 indeed at the time of incident and that the injuries have been caused to the petitioner on account of the incident in question itself.

22. Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of R-1,
if any, in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. the offending car ) hit the vehicle of the petitioner.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner or any other such person, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

sentences.text: 23. In view of the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the injuries to the petitioner Sunita Vaid in the above accident.

24. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the injured Sunita Vaid suffered injuries on account of neglect and default of R1 while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
The issue at hand is thus decided against the respondents and in favour of the petitioner.
Issue no. (ii) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP. 
25.

On the basis of findings upon issue no. (i), it is clear that the incident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and injuries had been caused to the petitioner in the incident.
Hence, petitioner is entitled to compensation in this case.
26. The issue at hand is accordingly decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
LIABILITY 27.
Now the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Herein, it is pertinent to note that the respondent Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.02.06 14:24:35 +0530 no. 2 i.e. Insurance Company has specifically admitted in its written statement that the offending vehicle bearing registration no.
DL3CCN-6433 was duly insured at the time of accident with respondent no. 2 vide policy no. OG-21-4321- 1801-00000126, which was valid from 09.08.2020 to 08.08.2021.
Furthermore, the respondent no. 02 has failed to bring on record or to prove any breach of the terms or conditions of the said insurance policy by the respondents no.01 in any manner.

28. Hence, on the basis of entire above stated facts and circumstances and discussion of evidence,
this Tribunal is of the opinion that respondent no. 2 i.e. insurance company is liable to pay the entire compensation to the petitioner on behalf of respondent no. 1, without any recovery rights against the said respondent.

The evidence of the star witness in this case i.e. PW-1 & PW2 on the aspect of rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 while driving the offending vehicle, has remained unimpeached and their testimony has to be accepted on its face value itself.
Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
21.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that the offending vehicle was being driven by R-1 indeed at the time of incident and that the injuries have been caused to the petitioner on account of the incident in question itself.
Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. the offending car ) hit the vehicle of the petitioner.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner or any other such person, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
On the basis of findings upon issue no. (i), it is clear that the incident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and injuries had been caused to the petitioner in the incident.
Hence, petitioner is entitled to compensation in this case.
Furthermore, the respondent no. 02 has failed to bring on record or to prove any breach of the terms or conditions of the said insurance policy by the respondents no.01 in any manner.
